paper_summary: A theoretical/modelling paper that assembles existing micromechanics models (Gibson-Ashby for resin-impregnated paper honeycomb, Porfiri and Gupta's differential scheme for syntactic foam, and rule-of-mixtures/Halpin-Tsai for woven E-glass/epoxy face skins) into a modified classical lamination theory (MCLT) for foam-core sandwich composites. For the syntactic foam (dry fly ash cenospheres, mean diameter 150 um, radius ratio eta = 0.9, Vceno = 0.7272 in a phenolic resin matrix) the predicted Young's modulus is 1.99 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.25, shear modulus 0.796 GPa and density 654.54 kg/m3. The MCLT predictions for the syntactic-foam-core / E-glass-epoxy-skin sandwich (Ex = Ey = 4.469 GPa, Gxy = 1.0023 GPa, Gyz = Gxz = 0.9838 GPa) agree with experimental values reported earlier by Amith Kumar S.J. and Sabeel Ahmed within 1.9-5.2%.

extraction_notes: This is a purely analytical/review paper: no material was made or tested here, so no record is 'primary'. Model predictions are data_origin='model'; the experimental columns in Tables 6-7 are values reported earlier by the authors in ref [3] (Amith Kumar S.J., Sabeel Ahmed K., J. Reinforced Plastics and Composites 2013, 32, 1370-1379) and are therefore data_origin='secondary' with the citation in sample_label. CAVEAT on records 3-8: these are properties of the SANDWICH PANEL (syntactic foam core between woven E-glass/epoxy skins), not of the bare syntactic foam, so their moduli must not be read as foam moduli; sample_label flags this and the cenosphere volume fraction / core density fields were deliberately left null on those records (the fraction applies to the core only). Only records 1-2 describe the bare syntactic foam. Excluded from records: the resin-impregnated paper honeycomb core (Tables 1-3, samples N20/K20/K15/K10/K5) and the E-glass/epoxy face skin (Tables 5-6), because neither is a hollow-particle composite. Unit conversions: GPa x 1000 -> MPa (1.99 -> 1990, 0.796 -> 796, 4.469 -> 4469, 4.38 -> 4380, 1.0023 -> 1002.3, 0.961 -> 961, 0.9838 -> 983.8, 1.035 -> 1035); kg/m3 / 1000 -> g/cm3 (654.54 -> 0.65454 foam density, 450 -> 0.45 cenosphere true density). Ex = Ey and Gyz = Gxz in Table 7, so one record each rather than duplicates. Foam Poisson's ratio 0.25 (misprinted as '0.25 GPa' in the text) has no schema field and is kept in microstructure_notes. No strength, strain, energy-absorption or thermal data appear anywhere in the paper. Process route is 'other' because no fabrication route is described for the modelled foam.
